h1: The Pool Resort Bangkok — A Budget Pool Resort Just 0.3 km from Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital
intro: Finding affordable accommodation within easy reach of Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital — and still managing to have a decent pool to unwind beside after a long day — is harder than it sounds in Bangkok's eastern suburbs. The Pool Resort sits at 43/2 Soi Rama 9 Soi 57/1 in Suan Luang, just 0.3 km from Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital — a 3-minute drive, or a short walk on a cooler day. The small property has 22 rooms, an outdoor pool with a hot tub, a garden, a restaurant and bar, 24-hour room service, and free parking. Rooms start from around ฿650/night in low season and rise to roughly ฿1,100 in peak periods. The score is 7.3 from 20 reviews on Trip.com — not sparkling, but useful context: this is budget territory, the location advantage is real, and knowing the honest trade-offs lets you choose with open eyes.

body.html: The Pool Resort is tucked into a small soi off Rama 9 Road in Suan Luang, a residential and office district on Bangkok's east side that sees almost no tourists. What it does see is a steady flow of patient families coming and going from Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital, which sits just 0.3 km away on Srinakarin Road. That proximity is the hotel's defining argument: in this particular neighbourhood, being half a kilometre from the hospital entrance is genuinely difficult to improve on at any price, let alone at budget rates.

The 22 rooms are divided across Standard Double (29 sqm, double bed), Standard Twin (two single beds), Double with Pool View and King with Pool View. All come with air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a refrigerator, en-suite bathroom and free Wi-Fi. Reviewers consistently describe rooms as clean and smelling fresh, which matters more than it might seem when you are staying for medical reasons and spending most of your time inside. The room layout is functional rather than inspired — a budget resort, clearly — but the basics are covered.
"The pool was great — we swam in the evenings after visiting the hospital. Very quiet, staff were friendly and the price was fair. Close to Samitivej. Would use it again for hospital visits."

The headline feature — and the reason most guests give it a pass on the age of the fittings — is the outdoor swimming pool with hot tub (Jacuzzi), ringed by a garden, sun loungers and outdoor seating. The atmosphere is genuinely quiet. For families spending days in a hospital ward, being able to sit by a pool in the evenings is not nothing. The on-site restaurant covers breakfast, lunch and dinner, and room service runs around the clock. Free parking is available on-site, which matters if you are driving to appointments daily.

The honest picture from the reviews is this: some rooms show their age. Reviewers have noted ceiling damage, the occasional pigeon wandering onto the property, bathroom shower enclosures that let water overflow, and rooms with dim natural light. The rating breakdown on Trip.com reflects it — Facilities sits at 7.1, Cleanliness at 7.2. Some guests also reported noise from other guests on louder evenings, and a few noted communication difficulties with staff in unusual situations. These are real issues, not deal-breakers for the right traveller, but they deserve mention.

Transport in this part of Bangkok takes some planning. There is no rail station at the door: the closest is Airport Rail Link Hua Mak station, roughly 3.5 km away by Grab (around 10 minutes). The MRT Yellow Line's Sri Kritha station is about 2.5 km out. For the day-to-day hospital run, a Grab or short walk is perfectly workable. Seacon Square and The Nine Center — both with food courts, supermarkets and pharmacies — are within a 5–10 minute drive, which covers most practical needs during a longer stay.

The bottom line is straightforward: The Pool Resort fits one type of guest well — someone accompanying a patient at Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital who needs accommodation close by, is working within a limited budget, and values having a pool to decompress beside. The 7.3/10 score signals mixed experiences, so the advice is to look at the most recent photos on whichever platform you use and read the reviews from the past six months before booking. Go in with accurate expectations and it is likely to deliver what you need; go in expecting a polished resort and you will be disappointed.

honestSummary: The Pool Resort is one of the closest affordable options to Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital — 0.3 km, 3-minute drive — with a genuine outdoor pool and hot tub that guests consistently praise. The trade-off is a mixed review score reflecting inconsistent room condition and dated facilities. If proximity to the hospital and a low nightly rate are your priorities, and you check recent photos before booking, it delivers what it promises.
honestChecks: If you expect a polished, well-maintained room — guest reviews flag ceiling damage, dated fittings and maintenance gaps in some units. Check the most recent room photos on your booking platform and, at check-in, inspect before settling in.

If convenient public transport is important — there is no rail station near the hotel. The Airport Rail Link at Hua Mak is about 3.5 km away by Grab, and the MRT Yellow Line's Sri Kritha station is around 2.5 km. Budget for Grab or taxi costs throughout your stay.

If you are sensitive to noise — some reviewers experienced disturbances from other guests on livelier nights. Mention this at check-in and ask for a room away from common areas; staff are generally responsive.

tips.title: Getting to Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital
tips.body: Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital on Srinakarin Road is just 0.3 km away — a 2–3 minute drive or Grab. On a cooler day, the walk from Soi Rama 9 Soi 57/1 to the hospital entrance is manageable. The hotel is one of the few options in this area within a genuine 5-minute radius of the hospital.

tips.title: Getting around Bangkok from here
tips.body: No rail station is walkable from the hotel. Grab to Airport Rail Link Hua Mak station (3.5 km, ~10 min) connects you to Phaya Thai and Makkasan. The MRT Yellow Line at Sri Kritha station is about 2.5 km by Grab. For Suvarnabhumi Airport, a direct Grab takes 30–40 minutes.

tips.title: Food and shopping nearby
tips.body: Seacon Square and The Nine Center are 5–10 minutes by car, with restaurants, food courts, supermarkets and pharmacies. Local rice-and-curry shops and 24-hour convenience stores line Srinakarin Road and the Rama 9 sois — adequate for most daily needs during an extended stay.

tips.title: Check recent photos before you book
tips.body: Review scores are mixed partly because room condition varies. Look at photos uploaded within the last 6 months on your booking platform, and read the most recent guest reviews. At check-in, inspect the room before unpacking — staff are generally willing to swap if there is an obvious issue.

faq.q: Where is The Pool Resort Bangkok, and how far is it from Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital?
faq.a: The Pool Resort is at 43/2 Soi Rama 9 Soi 57/1, Suan Luang, Bangkok 10250. Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital on Srinakarin Road is just 0.3 km away — approximately a 3-minute drive or short walk. It is one of the closest hotels to the hospital in this area.

faq.q: What do rooms at The Pool Resort Bangkok cost?
faq.a: Rooms start from around ฿650/night for a Standard Double in low season. Pool View rooms (Double or King) run ฿800–950 per night. Prices rise to roughly ฿1,100 in peak season. Always compare across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before booking, as rates vary.

faq.q: Does The Pool Resort Bangkok have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor swimming pool with a hot tub (Jacuzzi), surrounded by a garden and sun loungers. This is the feature guests mention most positively in reviews, and it is what sets The Pool Resort apart from other budget options near Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital.

faq.q: How do I get from Suvarnabhumi Airport to The Pool Resort Bangkok?
faq.a: Suvarnabhumi Airport is about 20 km away — a 30–40 minute drive. The most direct option is a Grab from the airport to the hotel, costing roughly ฿300–400. Alternatively, take the Airport Rail Link to Hua Mak station, then a Grab for the final 3.5 km (about 10 minutes). The hotel does not offer its own airport shuttle.

faq.q: Is The Pool Resort Bangkok good for a long stay near the hospital?
faq.a: It works for a budget-focused long stay if you go in with clear expectations. The proximity to Samitivej Srinakarin Hospital (0.3 km) and the outdoor pool are genuine advantages. The limitations are room condition (some units show age) and a reliance on Grab for all transport. Check the latest photos and reviews on your platform before booking, and ask about room availability at check-in.
